Denmark’s prime minister blasts unsolicited beauty advice from plastic surgeon on Instagram
COPENHAGEN, Denmark (AP) — Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen is fed up with getting unsolicited beauty advice.
The 48-year-old wrote Monday on Instagram that she had just returned back home from a trip to Ukraine, where she was exposed to air raid sirens in the ongoing war, only to find a message by a plastic surgeon offering her to “fix that little spot on your nose.”
“I’ve lost count of how many messages I’ve received over the years about my appearance,” Frederiksen wrote. “Especially that I have ugly teeth and thin hair. That I have an ugly ‘wart’ on my nose and well-meaning advice to get some Botox.”
The prime minister of the Nordic country posted a screen shot of the plastic surgeon’s offer on Instagram but without identifying him.
She also posted her response: “Oh no. I’m happy with my body — I really don’t need a male plastic surgeon to have an opinion about it!”
Frederiksen, a Social Democrat and Denmark ’s second female prime minister, is now in her third term, making her one of Europe’s longest-serving and most experienced leaders. She has led the European Union and NATO member country since mid-2019.
She has pledged to maintain a firm stance against U.S. President Donald Trump’s ambitions for Greenland, the kingdom’s semiautonomous territory, and continue supporting Ukraine against Russia’s war of aggression.
On Instagram, Frederiksen stressed that she does not interfere with other people’s looks and that “I’m perfectly fine with my body — as it is when you’re a woman approaching 50.”
She added that “if you’re going to write to me (and you’re more than welcome to), I hope you’ll use your time to talk about something more meaningful. Not my nose.”
The prime minister also said that those unsolicited beauty tips and suggestions made her feel “indignant” and that “today, I’m sending an extra loving thought to all of you who have to put up with the ‘perfect imperfections’ we all walk around with every day.”

Gang coalition unleashes violent new attack on farming community in Haiti
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-24

Gang coalition unleashes violent new attack on farming community in Haiti
PORT-AU-PRINCE, Haiti (AP) — A powerful gang coalition attacked a once peaceful farming community nestled in the hills above Haiti’s capital, killing multiple people, an official told The Associated Press on Monday.
Kenscoff Mayor Jean Massillon said armed men raided the community late Sunday, setting fire to homes and killing residents.
“It is still impossible to establish a definitive death toll due to access difficulties and communication problems,” he said.
Wails filled the air in Kenscoff as survivors found the bodies of friends and family strewn on the streets early Monday.
“They killed my son!” one woman kept yelling as people nearby tried to comfort her.
One man flung himself on the side of the road, head on his right arm as he cried on the ground. Nearby, people picked up the bodies of those killed, some wrapped in blood-spattered sheets.
Robert Jean recalled how he heard shooting before dawn and tried to rouse people from their sleep to escape being killed. He said he was frantically looking for his brother, who was killed: “I was calling to see if everyone was safe. I could not find my brother.”
Another Kenscoff resident blamed the government for the killings.
“If only we had a good police force that would have placed an armored truck here, what happened here would have been prevented,” said Verti Enold-Saint as he lifted a sheet over the body of his brother-in-law.
Farmer Mathurin Pierre, 41, told AP that he lost 14 loved ones and that an unknown number remain missing.
Massillon blamed the attack on members of Viv Ansanm, which the U.S. government designated as a foreign terrorist organization last year.
“They sowed chaos,” Massillon said.
He said gang members targeted a church and homes including those owned by Dr. Jean “Bill” Pape. He is a renowned doctor who runs a nongovernmental organization in Haiti that helps patients including those with HIV and tuberculosis.
Haiti’s Office of Citizen Protection issued a statement decrying the massacre, saying dozens of people, including “numerous” young Haitians, were killed.
Vladimir Paraison, director of Haiti’s National Police, visited the area and defended police officers as journalists pressed for answers.
“The police never lowered their arms,” he said. “Look at how many police officers are here; the response is in front of you.”
Jean Fritz Patterson Dorval, head of Port-au-Prince’s prosecutor’s office, also came under pressure. He said there are eight armored vehicles in Kenscoff, adding that “there are technical responses that only the mayor and the police can answer.”
No further details about the attack were available. A spokesperson for the U.N.-backed gang suppression force did not return a message seeking comment.
Haiti’s government issued a statement condemning what it called a heinous criminal attack. “Reinforcements are being deployed,” it said. “Kenscoff will not be abandoned.”
It said that security forces were ordered to pursue those responsible. “The population must remain confident,” the government said, adding that it would not back down.
Gangs control an estimated 70% of Port-au-Prince, the capital, with Viv Ansanm repeatedly targeting nearby Kenscoff.
Gang violence has displaced a record 1.5 million people across Haiti, where more than 3,100 people were reported killed from January to June and another 1,189 injured, according to U.N. statistics.
The attack comes less than a week after the U.S. government deported more than 160 people to the troubled Caribbean country for the first time since the Trump administration won a legal battle to end Temporary Protected Status for some 350,000 Haitians.
Haiti’s government has said some of the deportees included TPS holders. The U.S. Department of Homeland Security said Monday in a statement to the AP that those deported Friday included several gang members with criminal records ranging from assault to drug trafficking.
Haiti is scheduled to hold general elections for the first time in more than a decade on Dec. 13, and it has been registering voters in Port-au-Prince and beyond. Experts have warned it’s currently too dangerous to hold elections.
___
Associated Press reporter Dánica Coto in San Juan, Puerto Rico, contributed.

2 UN peacekeepers killed in an ambush in South Sudan
Unknown
Unknown Publisher

Armed men ambush a patrol in South Sudan and kill 2 UN peacekeepers
JUBA, South Sudan (AP) — Armed men ambushed a patrol traveling to a remote area of South Sudan on Monday, killing two U.N. peacekeepers, the United Nations Mission in South Sudan said. Though violence is rampant in the African country, attacks against peacekeepers are rare.
No group immediately claimed responsibility for the attack. Seven others were wounded — three peacekeepers, two members of the South Sudanese police and two civilian staffers, the mission known as UNMISS said in a statement. The two peacekeepers killed and three injured were from Ethiopia, U.N. spokesperson Stéphane Dujarric said.
The mission said it had deployed a “Quick Reaction Force” to secure the area and support the emergency response after the attack. The patrol was going to the area of Pajut in the state of Jonglei when it came under attack.
“Such deadly violence targeting UNMISS personnel who are serving to support peace in South Sudan is unacceptable,” Anita Kiki Gbeho, the head of UNMISS, said in the statement.
The killings bring the number of peacekeepers killed by militias since Jan. 1 to nine, Dujarric said, stressing that attacks against U.N. peacekeepers may constitute war crimes under international law.
U.N. Secretary-General António Guterres condemned the ambush “in the strongest possible terms” and called for a prompt investigation that would lead to the prosecution of those responsible, Dujarric said later Monday.
“The secretary-general reaffirms the United Nations’ commitment to stand with the victims and their families during this profoundly difficult time,” the spokesman said.
Government troops in South Sudan have been combating fighters and militias loyal to opposition leader Riek Machar, who was suspended last year as vice president as he faces charges of treason and other offenses. Machar says the charges are politically motivated.
A 2018 peace deal between President Salva Kiir and Machar, who is under house arrest, has collapsed, leading to fears of a return to full-blown civil war.
Between January and July, more than 450 incidents of violence against humanitarian workers and assets were reported, more than double the number recorded during the same period last year, according to U.N. figures.
The conflict escalated in December when opposition forces seized government outposts in Jonglei. The government has been carrying out a counteroffensive since January, with aerial bombardments and ground assaults, despite an official commitment to the peace agreement.
The United States has urged for talks between Kiir and Machar. Earlier this year, it called for “urgent action to uphold peace and mitigate the risk of civil war through an immediate return to dialogue among the parties to the 2018 peace agreement.”

Associated Press writer Edith M. Lederer at the United Nations contributed to this report.

Former world snooker champion Graeme Dott convicted of sexually abusing children

Firefighters are trying to stop a fast-moving Nevada wildfire from spreading to homes in Reno
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-24
15:23:02 UTC
00:23:02 KST

Firefighters make progress against a Nevada wildfire that’s destroyed more than 30 homes
RENO, Nevada (AP) — Crews have started to contain a wildfire in the Sierra Nevada foothills near Reno, Nevada, that destroyed more than 30 homes as it spread perilously close to dense neighborhoods, officials said Monday.
Containment reached 27% and there was no new growth of the Hawk Fire, which has held steady at about 23 square miles (60 square kilometers) since it burned out of control on Sunday, authorities said at an afternoon news briefing.
“We are making progress,” said U.S. Forest Service District Ranger Matt Zumstein.
The number of residents under evacuation orders and warnings was reduced to about 63,000, down from more than 90,000 people when the blaze mushroomed over the weekend. While winds have eased, there’s still concern that gusts could push the flames through dry brush into newly developed neighborhoods in Nevada’s largest city outside of metro Las Vegas.
Firefighters are also contending with hot temperatures and low humidity. At least 32 homes have burned and six are damaged, but authorities said those numbers are sure to rise as assessment teams begin to survey the charred areas.
Reno Mayor Hillary Schieve said the way the fire spread so quickly at its height had her fearing for the worst.
“It lit up these areas like nothing I’ve seen before,” she said Monday. “It took your breath away, in the worst way.”
Hawk Fire triggers evacuations and school closures
Schools across Washoe County were closed Monday because of the evacuations and to keep roads clear for emergency crews. Nevada’s governor declared a state of emergency in the county and mobilized the National Guard to help with aerial firefighting and protecting evacuated neighborhoods northwest of downtown Reno.
At one roadblock, residents expressed frustration Monday that they could not get back into their homes.
“There’s no fire here! Why are the National Guard here?” a driver yelled.
Washoe County Sheriff Darin Balaam said he understands that some residents are frustrated that they can’t get home but the danger isn’t over yet. “It just takes that little breeze and one ember,” he said.
Wildfires near Reno are blamed on human activity
The fire near the California state line began Saturday and exploded in size on Sunday. At least seven people — three first responders and four civilians — have been injured.
This is the third large wildfire in the rugged terrain north of Reno in the past two weeks — all caused by human activity, according to fire officials. They haven’t said whether the Hawk Fire was intentionally set or accidental. Much of the area that burned was sagebrush and grass.
Reno, home to about 280,000 people, is known for its casinos and as a gateway to nearby Lake Tahoe, North America’s largest alpine lake and a popular vacation destination. It’s also southwest of Nevada’s Black Rock Desert, site of the annual Burning Man festival, which begins next Sunday.
Many who travel to Burning Man make Reno a regular stop. Organizers on Monday asked attendees to not take hotel rooms and other resources away from fire evacuees, while being mindful of closures.
“Treat our neighbors, first responders, hospitality workers and everyone affected by this emergency with patience and care,” a Burning Man statement said.
Fire claims a Reno woman’s home for a second time
Videos posted on social media showed the smoldering ruins of homes and cars, with only a scorched basketball hoop still standing.
Crystal Hallock, 53, lost her home to fire for a second time in less than a decade. She moved into the rebuilt house in 2019, a year after an electrical fire burned it down.
On Saturday, with a giant plume of smoke and flames visible on the nearby mountaintop, she fled with her children, grandchildren and pets. Her ex-husband tried to save the property and her vintage Cadillac, grabbing a garden hose as flames melted children’s toys and burned bushes.
She urged him over the phone to get out and feared the worst when the line went dead. “He was saying he can’t breathe, it’s so dark I can’t see, and I’m screaming at him, ‘Leave the car, just leave it,’” she said Monday.
Thirty minutes later, he called to say he had gotten out with the car. “I’m truly blessed because I have a place to stay with my animals and my grandkids. We were all able to get out safely,” she said from a niece’s apartment in Reno.
Nevada fire spread quickly in foothills
Many residents had little time to evacuate after the fire exploded in size.
“Honestly, I thought it was like in a movie,” said Ruby Delatorre, who got back from a concert only to find her home in the evacuation zone. She returned Sunday to walk to her house and get a few more possessions.
“I literally want to cry and go back for all my stuff. I just got what I thought I needed,” Delatorre said.
Some who spotted the smoke on Saturday thought it was from another wildfire that has been burning the past two weeks.
“The flames were pretty close to my house, and the smoke was really thick, but we have no idea if our house survived or not,” Jon Hanbury said Monday at Reno’s convention center, which is now a shelter.
Wildfire threat remains high in the West
Much of Nevada’s western edge is under an increased risk of wildfires this week because of high winds and low relative humidity, the National Interagency Fire Center said. The National Weather Service says the region will see warm, dry and breezy conditions, and that critical fire weather conditions are possible in the week’s later half. Reno sits at an elevation of 4,500 feet (1,370 meters).
Extremely dry conditions across the American West have sparked a rash of wildfires this summer. Fires in eastern Washington state forced the evacuation of 60,000 people in the Spokane area in early August.
Nationwide, there have been more than 50,000 wildfires — the most over the past 10 years covering the same time period, according to the national fire center.
___
Seewer reported from Toledo, Ohio. Associated Press writers Christopher Weber in Los Angeles, Martha Bellisle in Seattle, and Sudhin Thanawala in Atlanta contributed.

Smoke-free 2040 goal failing as young adults keep vaping
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-24
15:21:29 UTC
00:21:29 KST

Smoke-free 2040 goal failing as young adults keep vaping
See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results
A survey has suggested that four in ten young adults in the Netherlands smoke or vape, pointing to how far the country remains from its goal of a smoke-free generation by 2040.
Under the National Prevention Agreement, the government wants nobody in the younger generation to be smoking or vaping by then, and fewer than 5% of adults to do so.
The 40% figure comes from a poll of 2,000 people by comparison website Independer, which found the habit most common among 18-to-29-year-olds. The share drops to around 30% among people in their thirties, 17% among the over-45s and 10% among the over-60s.
Independer is a commercial comparison site rather than a statistical agency, and its figure is well above official data. National statistics agency CBS put the proportion of 18-to-25-year-olds who smoke or vape at roughly a quarter in 2024.
Doctors want a ban
 Paediatric lung specialist Noor Rikkers, of the Artsen slaan alarm (doctors sound the alarm) campaign group, called the numbers shocking and said the rise of vaping was drawing in ever-younger children.
She wants the government to ban all products that contain nicotine, arguing that a blanket ban would be simpler to enforce than the current patchwork of rules.
Social media a factor
 The survey also pointed to social media. About three-quarters of young adults said they saw videos of people smoking or vaping, and a third of those said the clips tempted them to try it.
More than a quarter of the young smokers who watched such videos said they bought cigarettes or vapes through social media, even though online and social-media sales of tobacco and vapes have been banned since 2023 – a rule dealers have been flouting on Snapchat.
Flavoured vapes have been banned since January 2024, but doctors and inspectors say a black market keeps supplying illegal products.

In Ukraine, stamps titled &quot;We Are Waiting!&quot; were issued for Independence Day in support of prisoners of war
Ukraine
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-24
18:20:58 EEST
00:20:58 KST

In Ukraine, stamps titled "We Are Waiting!" were issued for Independence Day in support of prisoners of war
Kyiv • UNN
Ukrposhta issued two stamps for the 35th anniversary of Independence in support of prisoners of war and missing persons. They were chosen by nearly 328,800 people.
For the 35th anniversary of Ukraine’s independence, Ukrposhta, together with the Coordination Headquarters for the Treatment of Prisoners of War, issued the "We Are Waiting!" postage stamps as a sign of support for Ukrainian prisoners of war, missing persons, and their families, UNN reports, citing Ukrposhta.
Details
Ukraine is marking its fifth Independence Day during the full-scale war thanks to the people who stood up to defend it. Some of them are still being held captive in Russia, while the fate of others remains unknown. Their relatives, friends, fellow soldiers — and the entire country for whose independence they fought — are waiting for them.
The postage issue consists of two stamps — "Stork. Freedom" by artist Nikita Titov and "Messenger of Good News" by Andriy Yermolenko. Both works are about waiting, hope, and freedom that cannot be taken away.
"Stork. Freedom" depicts a bird with wings in the colors of the Flag of Hope, a symbol of support for prisoners of war and missing persons. White represents faith in their return, while black represents the unknown. The stork, which always returns home, symbolizes the return awaited by thousands of Ukrainian families.
On "Messenger of Good News," a prisoner of war’s hand reaches through the bars toward a tit, a symbol of good news. Even in captivity, Ukrainian soldiers preserve the spirit of freedom. And this postage issue will carry the most important message from home around the world: you are awaited here. In a free and independent Ukraine.
Ukrainians chose both designs during an open vote in the "Diia" app, in which nearly 328.8 thousand people took part.
A ceremony for the special cancellation of the new postage stamps was held at the Main Post Office with the participation of the leadership of Ukrposhta, the Main Intelligence Directorate, the Ministry of Digital Transformation, and families of prisoners of war and those released from Russian captivity. Events were held simultaneously in all regions of Ukraine.
On August 24, an exhibition of portraits of Ukrainian servicemen who returned from Russian captivity also opened at the Main Post Office. It will run for a week. Alongside the postage symbols honoring those who are still awaited, the faces of those who have returned home have appeared.
"Independence Day is a bright holiday. But even on this day — or rather, precisely on this day — we must remember those who have done and continue to do everything to defend our independence. Those who are currently being held captive in Russia, and those considered missing.
For them and their families, every indication that they are remembered, awaited, and that efforts to secure their return continue is extremely important. Starting today, hundreds of thousands of our stamps will spread across Ukraine and the world to remind us again and again: we remember each and every one. And we are waiting for each and every one to come home," said Ihor Smilianskyi, CEO of JSC "Ukrposhta."
The print run of each of the two postage stamps is 360,000 copies. Both have a denomination of U.
A "First Day" envelope designed by Oleksii Kustovskyi, with a print run of 25,000 copies, and a presentation folder with a print run of 500 copies were also created for the issue. The stamps were printed using the offset method.

Indonesia’s Ministry of Forestry and Vantara, founded by Anant Ambani, Executive Director of Reliance Industries Limited, have announced a partnership focused on strengthening wildlife health infrastructure, veterinary care and conservation efforts in Indonesia.The programme will include training for elephant caregivers, veterinarians and officials involved in wildlife management, along with 10 veterinary hospitals, or ‘Hospitals on Wheels’ for wild animals across Indonesia. The Way Kambas Elephant Hospital will be upgraded into an Elephant Treatment and Care Centre with equipment and technology.
The upgraded facility is expected to support 62 Sumatran elephants under human care and nearly 100 wild Sumatran elephants in the surrounding landscape, according to the announcement.The programme is part of a Memorandum of Understanding between the Indonesian government and Vantara covering wildlife health, animal welfare and conservation. The cooperation also includes conservation breeding, rehabilitation, rewilding, in situ and ex situ conservation, and capacity building.
Vantara will provide veterinary expertise, technical support, infrastructure assistance and training in programmes led by Indonesian authorities, working with national institutions and Fauna Land.
Indonesia’s Forestry Minister Raja Juli Antoni said the cooperation would strengthen the country’s ability to care for wildlife while ensuring that the programmes remain under Indonesian authorities.“Wildlife conservation is ultimately our responsibility, and we must ensure that Indonesia has the facilities, expertise and resources to care for our wildlife wherever they need us. Through this partnership, we are strengthening our own wildlife health and conservation infrastructure, with Vantara supporting us with its experience, expertise and resources,” Antoni said.Vantara CEO Vivaan Karani said the organisation would share its experience in wildlife health, veterinary care, animal husbandry and conservation while also learning from Indonesia’s conservation work.
“Indonesia is home to some of the world's most extraordinary biodiversity, and it is a privilege for Vantara to support the country in protecting this heritage for future generations,” Karani said. “Most importantly, we want this partnership to deliver something practical and lasting for wildlife.”Faunaland CEO Danny Gunalen said the partnership could help strengthen local capacity and wildlife infrastructure.“Indonesia is blessed with extraordinary wildlife and biodiversity, and protecting this natural heritage is a responsibility we all share,
” Gunalen said. “We hope this partnership will build local capacity, strengthen the infrastructure available to wildlife and, most importantly, make a real and lasting difference to the animals and the people dedicated to protecting them.”The cooperation will follow Indonesia’s national conservation priorities and applicable laws and policies, with its success ultimately measured by how effectively the new support reaches animals in need and translates into stronger, lasting protection for endangered species across the country.

Volkswagen unveiled new Tukan pickup, which will replace Saveiro

Volkswagen unveiled new Tukan pickup, which will replace Saveiro
Kyiv • UNN
Volkswagen has introduced the Tukan pickup in Brazil with single- and double-cab configurations. Sales will begin in early 2027, while the Saveiro will be discontinued.
Volkswagen has finally unveiled the all-new Tukan in Brazil without camouflage. Developed to replace the long-running Saveiro, the new pickup was first shown to the public at the Barretos Rodeo festival in the state of São Paulo, Brazil, in single- and double-cab variants. Sales are scheduled to begin in early 2027, reports UNN , citing Motor1.com.
Details
Larger and more modern than the Saveiro, the Tukan will be produced in São José dos Pinhais, Brazil, and will primarily compete with the Fiat Strada. VW has not yet released data on dimensions, payload capacity, or equipment. However, the two cab configurations suggest the availability of both work-oriented versions and better-equipped models intended for family use.
Although it was initially expected to become a direct competitor to the Fiat Toro, the Volkswagen Tukan will be closer in size to the Chevy Montana. Its task is to occupy the niche between compact and midsize pickups while also serving commercial buyers traditionally covered by the Saveiro.
The single-cab body will compete with more affordable versions of the Fiat Strada, offering a larger bed and a greater emphasis on cargo transportation. The double-cab model, meanwhile, is expected to offer turbocharged engines, automatic transmissions, and more extensively equipped configurations, broadening VW's appeal among buyers who also use their pickup as a personal vehicle.
The design follows the visual identity of VW's latest models. At the front, narrow headlights are connected by a horizontal strip, while the bumpers feature pronounced shapes and elements that emphasize the width of the body. At the rear, the taillights feature lighting in the shape of the letter "E" and are connected by a crossbar running across the full width of the tailgate.
VW is still keeping the technical specifications secret, but the Tukan is expected to offer different powertrains depending on the version. Base trims are expected to retain the familiar naturally aspirated 1.6 MSI engine with a manual transmission — a simple and more affordable combination aimed at corporate buyers and small producers.
Mid-level versions may receive a 1.0 TSI flex-fuel engine paired with a six-speed automatic transmission — or may even feature the new eight-speed gearbox recently introduced in the T-Cross. At the top of the range, the pickup is expected to debut in Brazil with the new 1.5 TSI Evo2 engine and a 48-volt mild-hybrid system, a technology that could later be extended to other models of the brand produced at the local plant.
The architecture will be based on the MQB platform, which is already used in the Polo, Nivus, Tera, and T-Cross. However, at the rear, engineers opted for a solid axle with leaf springs — a common construction for trucks that is also used by the competing Fiat Strada. This layout should provide greater payload capacity and durability in commercial use.
The arrival of the Tukan will also mark the end of the Saveiro.
Production is expected to end in the last quarter of 2026, making room in the lineup for the new pickup.

Helium balloon triggers explosions, train disruptions at Ben Gurion | Watch
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-24
15:19:50 UTC
00:19:50 KST

A helium balloon drifted into the railway station at Ben Gurion International Airport on Monday afternoon, causing electrical cables to short circuit and producing several loud bangs that disrupted train service at the country’s main international airport.
Passengers reported hearing explosions before people on the platform were directed into the airport terminal. Platform 2 was temporarily closed to train traffic following the incident.
Israel Railways described the incident as a localized technical malfunction that was being repaired. Some trains halted their journeys before reaching their final destinations, while others were delayed.
“There was a localized malfunction that is currently being handled. Trains are running,” Israel Railways said. “There may be delays in the near future, but train traffic has not been halted.”
The company disputed reports that the airport railway station had been evacuated, saying it “was not evacuated of passengers and continues normal operations.”
‘There were three explosions’
One passenger who contacted ynet said an electrical cable had been severed and that the 3:09 p.m. train from Jerusalem to Herzliya became stranded several minutes before reaching Ben Gurion Airport.
“There was no electricity or air conditioning for 10 minutes,” the passenger said, adding that passengers were later informed that the train would return to Jerusalem.
Another passenger said the train stopped at the station before three loud explosions were heard. “They have now evacuated everyone from the platform to the terminal,” the passenger said.
Alex, who was aboard one of the trains at the time, told ynet that his train had already arrived at the airport station when he heard several explosions.
“We stopped at the station and then there were several sounds of explosions, and the cable for the train opposite us snapped and fell,” he said. “There were flashes of light from an electrical short circuit and then another explosion. They then announced over the public-address system that we had to evacuate the train and led everyone into Ben Gurion Airport.”
Because of the resulting disruptions, Alex left the station and continued his journey by bus.
A senior Israel Railways official offered a stark assessment of the incident, warning that the railway had repeatedly narrowly avoided a serious accident.
“Every time, only an obvious miracle saves civilians from a deadly disaster,” the official told ynet. “But everyone knows that even obvious miracles run out one day. Once again, they will look for a scapegoat to blame. The disaster will come; only the date is unknown.”
Leadership vacuum at Israel Railways
The disruption comes as Israel Railways, the state-owned company that operates the country’s passenger and freight rail network, has been without its two most senior permanent executives for nearly two months: a board chairman and a CEO.
Moshe Shimoni, who served as chairman for about six years, left the position last month after being appointed chairman of Mekorot, Israel’s national water company.
Meanwhile, nearly a year after CEO Moshe “Shiko” Zana left the railway, a permanent replacement has yet to be appointed. Avner Flor, a former head of the Transportation Ministry’s infrastructure administration, is serving as acting CEO.
Industry officials say the difficulty in filling the CEO position is unsurprising because it is considered one of the most complex management jobs in Israel’s public sector.
Along with overseeing infrastructure projects worth tens of billions of shekels, the railway’s chief executive must contend with a powerful workers union, operational failures that frequently cause service disruptions, safety incidents and accidents, as well as persistent public criticism over the quality and reliability of train service.
Years of management upheaval
Israel Railways has experienced significant management turnover in recent years.
During Shimoni’s tenure as chairman, two CEOs were replaced, while a string of senior executives left the company, including its chief financial officer, legal adviser, head of human resources and head of the railway electrification administration.
More recently, the executive responsible for freight operations was removed from his position following two freight-train accidents.
The company has also faced delays to its electrification program, the end of its contract with Spanish infrastructure company SEMI and operational challenges during the war with Iran.
The upheaval comes at a particularly consequential period for Israel’s railway network, which is preparing to operate and complete some of the largest infrastructure projects in its history.
They include the Eastern Railway, the Route 431 railway, a fourth track through Tel Aviv’s heavily congested Ayalon rail corridor and completion of the nationwide electrification project.
For now, Israel Railways continues to operate under interim leadership at a time when it is expected to carry out its most ambitious development plans while also working to restore public confidence in the reliability and safety of its service.

Experts urge focus on harm, loss of control in tackling gaming addiction
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-24
15:19:36 UTC
00:19:36 KST

Spending hours in front of a screen does not, by itself, make someone addicted to gaming.
A player can spend long periods gaming, streaming or using social media without losing control or suffering serious consequences, while another person who spends less time online may see school performance decline, relationships deteriorate or psychological distress begin to take over.
That distinction is becoming increasingly important as researchers, parents and policymakers try to determine where intense engagement ends and harmful behavior begins.
For behavioral addiction researcher and psychologist Maeva Flayelle, there is no simple numerical answer.
Speaking about the challenges of identifying problematic gaming behavior, Flayelle said there is no fixed number of hours that separates healthy gaming from addiction.
“There is clearly no consensus on this matter,” she told Anadolu.
“There is no quantitative threshold to determine what is too much related to gaming,” Flayelle added.
She said some people may spend large amounts of time gaming, streaming or using social media without experiencing harmful consequences.
“You can have really highly engaged people in gaming, streaming or social media use, yet they don't encounter any negative consequences or they don't have any loss of control with that,” she said.
At the same time, Flayelle said someone who spends less time gaming may still experience significant problems.
“You can have people who will game a bit less, but who will have significant psychological distress and functional impairment in some domains of their lives,” she said, citing work, personal relationships and social relationships as examples.
“So, this is not a question of hours or amount of hours. This is really a question of outcomes and consequences in people's lives,” she said.
Flayelle said one of the main distinctions between ordinary gaming and problematic behavior is whether a person can continue to control how they engage with games.
“We can draw the line when people start to lose control over the time they spend gaming,” she said.
Repeated unsuccessful efforts to reduce gaming can also indicate a problem, she added.
Flayelle said the situation becomes more concerning when gaming is accompanied by “psychological distress” and negative feelings such as “guilt or regret.”
“Yet, we start to enter this problematic area,” she said.
Flayelle also pointed to the way video games are designed, particularly the use of loot boxes, as an area requiring closer scrutiny.
“We know more and more that loot boxes can cause some issues and cause some prolonged involvement with potential loss of control,” she said.
She said regulatory developments are already taking place and argued that current evidence gives policymakers reason to pay attention to the feature.
“With the evidence that we have today, loot boxes seem to be a design feature for which we should have attention in regulatory terms,” she said.
Young people require particular attention because of their stage of development, according to Flayelle.
“Of course, young people are a vulnerable group,” she said.
“We need to pay attention to them because, in terms of brain maturity, we still need to develop, notably for functions that underlie decision-making and self-regulation,” she added.
Flayelle said parents should not focus solely on screen time but should look more closely at what their children play, how they play and whether gaming is affecting other areas of their lives.
“Parents should monitor which games they play and how they play, and most importantly, they need to monitor whether there are some negative outcomes again in their lives,” she said.
She pointed to social isolation and declining school performance as possible warning signs.
“If you have a young individual who starts to isolate himself in the bedroom, always playing, there are no more social relationships, or the school grades are really decreasing,” she said.
“These are warning signals that parents should pay attention to.”
Flayelle said gaming disorder has received increasing attention from policymakers and regulators following its official recognition by the World Health Organization.
But she said researchers also need greater cooperation from gaming companies.
“What we need most today is probably to be able to enter a dialogue with the industry, with the gaming industry,” she said.
Researchers need access to industry data to improve studies of gaming behavior, she said.
“We would need, as researchers, to access their data to improve the research that we conduct on those behaviors,” Flayelle said.
She added that gaming companies also need to take greater responsibility.
“They also need to acknowledge that they probably should take greater responsibility for the way these video games are designed to prevent harms for users,” she said.
While Flayelle focused on identifying and preventing gaming-related harm, psychiatrist Jon Grant addressed how behavioral addictions can be treated once they become problematic.
Grant said researchers have conducted several double-blind, placebo-controlled trials over approximately 25 years examining treatments for behavioral addictions.
“I think the evidence base is good; it's not great,” Grant said.
Behavioral addictions differ from substance-related disorders because they do not involve consuming an external substance, raising questions about what medication should target.
Grant said treatment may depend on whether a patient is dealing only with the problematic behavior or also has other co-occurring conditions.
“If the person has no other problems, you can target the behavior itself,” he said.
“If they have these other co-occurring problems, that might mean that they may need two different medications or a slightly different medication based on whichever the co-occurring problem is,” he added.
Grant said he would like medication to become part of standard treatment alongside psychological approaches.
“I hope that they become a standard treatment along with psychotherapy,” he said.
“If we believe that these behavioral addictions are serious, then it seems as if we should do everything possible to help people with them.”
For Grant, that means clinicians should not necessarily view medication and psychotherapy as competing treatment options.
“And if that includes a combination of medication and psychotherapy, why wouldn't we do both?” he said.

Israel subjecting Russian historian to brutal interrogation – lawyer

Israel subjecting Russian historian to brutal interrogation – lawyer
Russian-Israeli historian Artyom Kirpichenok has been subjected to brutal treatment while in Shin Bet custody, including interrogations lasting up to 24 hours, sleep deprivation, prolonged handcuffing, and threats, according to his lawyer.
Kirpichenok, 51, disappeared on August 2 shortly after arriving at Ben Gurion Airport from Yerevan. His whereabouts remained unknown for nearly three weeks before his supporters revealed that he was being held at a detention facility in Petah Tikva.
His lawyer, Inna Lebedinskaya-Katz, was finally allowed to meet with him for around an hour on Sunday after repeatedly seeking access, according to Nika Dubrovsky, a Russian-born artist and writer campaigning for his release.
Citing Lebedinskaya-Katz, Dubrovsky said Kirpichenok has faced interrogation sessions lasting 18 to 24 hours while deprived of sleep. He is allegedly being kept handcuffed and hunched over on an iron stool fixed to the floor, with three or four interrogators standing behind him “shouting, threatening, and applying constant pressure.” He has also allegedly been threatened with life imprisonment.
Kirpichenok is in “tolerable physical condition” and has no immediate health complaints, but is “exhausted, tormented and deeply depressed,” Dubrovsky wrote on X on Monday.
”He understands that his friends have not abandoned him. He is holding on and sends his greetings to everyone,” she wrote. Kirpichenok also asked that no one come to Israel.
The allegations have not been independently verified. However, international human rights groups previously documented sleep deprivation and painful restraint during Shin Bet interrogations. Israel’s Supreme Court has ruled against deliberately using prolonged sleep deprivation to break suspects.
Kirpichenok is being held underground with the lights on around the clock and denied books and writing materials, Dubrovsky cited his lawyer as saying. A gag order remains in force, and the defense has yet to receive the case files or details of the accusations.
Kirpichenok, a dual Russian-Israeli citizen and Middle East expert, is known for criticizing Israel’s policies toward Iran and Palestine. Moscow sought information from the Israeli authorities following his disappearance and said it is closely monitoring the case.
Kirpichenok recently worked with media outlets and civic organizations in Türkiye and Iran and frequently traveled to Iran. Israeli citizens are generally prohibited from traveling to countries they are at war with. Dubrovsky, however, said the trips now appear to be of little interest to investigators.
Born in Russia, Kirpichenok moved to Israel in the 1990s, studied at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem and served in the Israel Defense Forces before returning to Russia. He later became a vocal critic of the Israeli government and its military campaign in Gaza, describing Israel as a Western “colonial project” in his recent book ‘Israel: The Road to Catastrophe’.
The Israeli authorities have yet to publicly disclose any charges against him.

Regulation on recognising foreign same-sex marriages comes into force in Poland
Unknown

2026-08-24

Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work!
Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support.
All registry offices in Poland can now recognise same-sex marriages conducted in other European Union countries, after a government regulation issued in May went into force. The decision came in response to a ruling by the Court of Justice of the EU (CJEU) requiring Poland to recognise such unions.
Deputy prime minister Krzysztof Gawkowski expressed his “great joy, because finally in Poland we have a law that gives the right to dignity”. The government’s plenipotentiary for equality, Katarzyna Kotula, warned local authorities that they will be breaking the law if they refuse to comply with the new rules.
However, the mayor of one town in a conservative region has already declared that his administration will not recognise such marriages. He argues that doing so would violate Poland’s constitution, which mentions marriage as a union between a man and a woman.

Nowe wzory aktów małżeństwa umożliwią transkrypcję zagranicznych aktów małżeństw jednopłciowych z pełnym szacunkiem dla par. To koniec administracyjnej fikcji i niepewności, z którą przez lata… pic.twitter.com/mRZYkEg9W4
— Krzysztof Gawkowski (@KGawkowski) August 22, 2026
Polish domestic law still does not allow any form of same-sex unions to be formed. However, last year, the CJEU ordered that the country recognise same-sex marriages conducted in other EU member states. That was followed by a similar ruling from Poland’s own Supreme Administrative Court (NSA).
One obstacle to implementing those decisions was that, previously, Poland’s civil registry only allowed male-female marriages to be entered. But, under a regulation issued by the government in May, the system now allows either mixed-sex or same-sex marriages.
Even before that went into force on Sunday, some Polish cities, starting with Warsaw and Wrocław, had already begun transcribing same-sex marriages conducted abroad into their registries. They simply listed one spouse in the “man” section and the other as a “woman”, even though that was not accurate for one of them.
But some local authorities have refused to do so, pointing to article 18 of Poland’s constitution, which states that: “Marriage, being a union of a man and a woman, as well as the family, motherhood and parenthood, shall be placed under the protection and care of the Republic of Poland.”
Such doubts were cited by the mayor of Zakopane, a town in southern Poland, last week when he announced that his administration did not intend to begin recognising foreign same-sex marriages after the regulation came into force.
“We will not be issuing such transcriptions in Zakopane,” said Łukasz Filipowski, quoted by local news service Nasze Miasto. He argued that doing so would “not be in accordance with the constitution”, adding that, while Zakopane is “tolerant”, it “promotes the traditional family model…[as] our foundation”.
Filipowski pointed to a ruling in July by the Constitutional Tribunal (TK), which found that the government’s regulation conflicts with the constitution’s definition of marriage. However, the government considers the TK to be improperly constituted and therefore regards its rulings as invalid.
Poland's Constitutional Tribunal has ruled that a new regulation allowing foreign same-sex marriage certificates to be registered in Poland is unconstitutional.
The government says it will not implement the rulinghttps://t.co/xDAzLjcJQ4
— Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) July 28, 2026
In response to Filipowski’s remarks, Kotula told broadcaster TVN that officials who refuse to recognise foreign same-sex marriages “will be breaking the law”. She said that the personal views of officials cannot “translate into what [legal] actions they take” and that the government would be monitoring the situation.
Gawkowski – who, like Kotula, is a leading figure in The Left (Lewica), a junior member of Poland’s ruling coalition – also warned municipalities against issuing refusals. He noted that, as well as the CJEU ruling, Polish courts have also issued orders to recognise foreign same-sex marriages.
“In the end, these local authorities will lose [a court battle], so why embarrass themselves? Let’s not look for legal tricks. Let’s just implement something that has been done in other, normal countries for years,” Gawkowski told Polsat News.
However, even once same-sex marriages are transcribed into Polish civil registries, there remains uncertainty about what legal consequences that will have in practice, especially given that Poland’s domestic law does not allow for any legally recognised form of same-sex union.
Legal experts say that it may take years – and potentially many more legal challenges by same-sex couples – for the situation to be clarified.
Separately, parliament earlier this year approved a bill, proposed by the ruling coalition, that would have granted same-sex couples in Poland certain rights normally granted to married couples. However, the law was vetoed by President Karol Nawrocki, who is aligned with the right-wing opposition.

Iran warns of retaliation against countries backing new US sanctions
Finland
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-24
18:18:40 EEST
00:18:40 KST

The United States is preparing a new sanctions campaign against Iran as Tehran threatens to stop oil exports from the Gulf and retaliate against countries that support Washington. The measures come six months into the US-Israeli war against Iran, with shipping through the Strait of Hormuz restricted and diplomatic efforts under way.
US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent is due to announce the measures on Monday.
He described the planned campaign as an “economic D-Day” and said Washington intends to sever Iran’s remaining sources of revenue.
Writing in the Financial Times, Bessent said the US would launch “the single greatest financial offensive ever marshalled against an adversary”. His comments indicate that Washington plans to pursue companies and countries that continue trading with Tehran, including through secondary sanctions.
The approach puts China at the centre of the dispute. Beijing is Iran’s largest trading partner and buys most of its exported oil. China reported $9.96bn in two-way trade with Iran in 2025, excluding about $31.2bn in Iranian oil shipments, according to figures from the US-China Economic and Security Review Commission.
The US Treasury estimates that China accounts for about 90 per cent of Iranian oil sales.
Washington has sanctioned several Chinese and Hong Kong companies over their links to Iranian oil. Major Chinese financial institutions have so far avoided direct US measures.
China’s Foreign Ministry said on Monday that sanctions and pressure would not resolve the conflict and said Beijing would protect Chinese interests. Wider action against Chinese companies would also come one month before US President Donald Trump is scheduled to host Chinese President Xi Jinping at the White House on 24 September.
Iran has responded to the US plans with warnings covering oil exports, shipping and states that assist Washington.
Mohsen Rezaei, secretary of Iran’s Supreme National Security Council, said Tehran would stop oil shipments throughout the Gulf if the economic campaign continued.
“If the economic war continues, not a single drop of oil will be exported, neither through the Strait of Hormuz nor from anywhere in the Persian Gulf,” Rezaei wrote on X.
He said Iran would regard participation in the US campaign as an act of war.
Iran’s Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei repeated that warning on Monday. He said countries that provide bases, facilities or equipment for attacks against Iran risk retaliation.
“There is no reason for any country to have concerns about Iran, unless it has made its bases, facilities, and equipment available to the aggressors,” Baghaei said in a press conference, according to Iranian media outlet Press TV.
Tehran has also tightened its position over the Strait of Hormuz, after US violations of an MoU signed in June. Iran’s Persian Gulf Strait Authority warned that vessels breaching its transit arrangements face fines, detention, confiscation or restrictions on subsequent journeys.
Traffic through the waterway remains low. Kpler data showed that 13 vessels crossed on Saturday and four on Sunday. Some ships had switched off their transponders, meaning the total number remains uncertain.
The security risks also extend beyond Hormuz. A projectile struck a tanker about 117km west of Yanbu, Saudi Arabia, on Monday and started a fire on its main deck, according to the UK Maritime Trade Operations. UKMTO said the crew remained safe. No group immediately claimed responsibility.
The economic pressure comes as Iran deals with inflation, currency losses and disruption caused by the war and restrictions on trade. The International Monetary Fund expects Iran’s economy to contract by 5.4 per cent in 2026.
The rial fell to about two million to the US dollar on Tehran’s open market on Sunday, Al Jazeera reported. Iranian government data released in July showed prices running 88 per cent above their level a year earlier, while food inflation exceeded 128 per cent.
President Masoud Pezeshkian acknowledged the economic pressure in a speech on Sunday. “I understand we have many problems in society right now,” he said, while accusing Washington of conducting an economic, military and security war.
Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi dismissed Washington’s sanctions threat as “desperate” and said Tehran remained prepared for negotiations based on terms acceptable to Iran.
The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps has also said it has prepared responses to further economic measures. IRGC spokesman Hossein Mohebbi said on Sunday that Iran had developed plans to maintain trade despite US restrictions.
Diplomatic activity continued alongside the threats. Pakistan’s army chief, Field Marshal Asim Munir, arrived in Tehran on Monday for meetings with Iranian officials. Pakistan said the visit formed part of its efforts to promote regional peace. Reuters reported, citing a Pakistani source, that Munir was expected to meet figures close to Iran’s supreme leader.
Omani Foreign Minister Badr Albusaidi is due in Tehran on Tuesday for talks covering Hormuz and regional security. Oman has maintained contacts with Iran as efforts continue to establish arrangements for the strait.
The US and Iran have not exchanged direct military strikes for several weeks, but formal face-to-face negotiations have stalled since June.
The conflict began when the United States and Israel launched illegal attacks on Iran on February 28, 2026, in the middle of ongoing negotiations. A memorandum of understanding was signed on June 17, 2026, but it was soon undermined by U.S. violations of its commitments, leading to the breakdown of the agreement and a renewed escalation of hostilities. The Strait of Hormuz was open and free before the US/Israeli aggression.

UK to help Ukraine build Storm Shadow long-range missiles: Why it matters
Unknown

2026-08-24

UK to help Ukraine build Storm Shadow long-range missiles: Why it matters
The UK’s willingness to share classified missile-production knowledge sets a potentially important precedent.
The United Kingdom is set to share classified weapons information with Ukraine to enable it to produce its own version of the Storm Shadow long-range cruise missile, designed jointly with France, as Prime Minister Andy Burnham visits Kyiv on his first foreign trip as the UK’s prime minister.
Burnham’s trip on Monday, timed to coincide with Ukraine’s 35th anniversary of independence from the Soviet Union, is the latest show of support on the part of the UK and Ukraine’s other European allies at a time when backing from the United States has been erratic, analysts said.
Recommended Stories
list of 3 items
- list 1 of 3Russia, Ukraine trade attacks as Putin warns of ‘far more destructive’ hits
- list 2 of 3Putin warns Ukraine has opened ‘Pandora’s box’, rejects peace proposals
- list 3 of 3Zelenskyy says wartime elections could ‘destroy’ Ukraine
Burnham described Russia’s war on Ukraine as “four and a half years of Russia’s full-scale invasion … aimed at crushing the independence we are here to celebrate” as he appeared alongside Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy at a ceremony in Kyiv.
“But today and every day, you prove that they have failed.”
Burnham is also to co-chair a meeting of the so-called Coalition of the Willing, those nations prepared to provide support for war-torn Ukraine.
The sharing of top-secret weapons blueprints stands in contrast to US President Donald Trump’s backpedalling last month on a promise to allow Ukraine to manufacture its own version of the US-made Patriot air defence interceptor, which Ukraine says it badly needs to counter Russian ballistic missile attacks.
While the US has provided Ukraine with US-made Patriot air defence batteries and munitions in the past, Trump last month said handing over the underlying technology to Ukraine to be able to independently produce them was “a hard thing to give away”.
The UK’s decision to share blueprints, however, follows a similar move by France and comes as Ukraine and Russia exchange heavy air attacks and Russian President Vladimir Putin warns of intensified retaliatory strikes on Ukrainian economic infrastructure.
Ukraine has stepped up its domestic military production, crafting long-range drones and missiles that strike deep into Russian territory, but analysts said producing its own Storm Shadows will give Kyiv the ability to hit Russia’s strategic targets more efficiently and at an unprecedented rate.
What are Storm Shadow long-range missiles?
Also known as SCALP in France, these missiles have a range of about 560km (350 miles) and are capable of hitting targets 240km (150 miles) inside Russian territory. This is not as far as Ukraine’s in-house, deep-strike drones, such as the FP-5 Flamingo cruise missile, which has a range of 3,000km (1,865 miles).
But while Ukrainian long-range missiles can hit “soft” targets inside Russia, such as Wildberries warehouses, Storm Shadow missiles give Kyiv the ability to hit “hard” targets, including heavily fortified, guarded locations that are usually protected by much tougher defences.
Their advanced navigation systems also mean they can be used at night and in all weather conditions.
Last year, the Ukrainian military’s General Staff said Storm Shadow missiles made by the manufacturer MBDA and provided by the UK had been used to hit Russian facilities, including a chemical plant and the Novoshakhtinsk oil refinery, one of the biggest oil product suppliers in southern Russia. This year, they were used to attack Russia’s Black Sea naval headquarters in the port city of Sevastopol in Crimea.
One Storm Shadow missile is estimated to cost about $1m to produce, so they are deployed in more carefully calibrated attacks than the flurry of cheap drones that Ukraine already mass-produces.
How easy will it be for Ukraine to build its own Storm Shadow missiles?
Keir Giles, an associate fellow at the Chatham House think tank, said Ukraine is likely to have a good capacity for producing these more sophisticated weapon systems once it has the blueprints.
“Ukraine, under the force of fighting a war of national survival, has been developing a very agile, highly motivated and distributed defence industry, which is far ahead in terms of adaptation to current needs [compared with] some of its Western European counterparts, including the UK,” he told Al Jazeera.
Being able to produce higher quantities of this missile, more than its actual capability, is what could make the difference, he added.
“Ukraine has had to be highly selective in the targets against which it uses its very limited stocks of the most advanced weapons systems,” Giles said. “Russia, meanwhile, has been exponentially increasing its production of drones and missiles, a trend that’s been in place for several years now.”
“So redressing that balance would be a major step forward for Ukraine, especially if it is able to reduce the number of missiles being launched at Ukraine every night by striking at the facilities that enable those launches,” the analyst added.
Has Ukraine been able to produce any of its own long-range missiles?
Yes. Besides its mass production of cheap short-range drones and interceptors, Ukraine is capable of designing and manufacturing more sophisticated longer-range missile systems, including the Neptune and Flamingo cruise missiles.
Karan Vassil, a Eurasia analyst at the UK-based private intelligence firm Sibylline, said Ukraine has also been developing and testing its own ballistic missile systems.
However, the Storm Shadow/SCALP “is a highly sophisticated weapons system incorporating decades of Anglo-French research and development”, Vassil told Al Jazeera. “Licensed production gives Ukraine access to knowledge and industrial processes that would otherwise take considerable time and resources to reproduce.”
Giles, who also leads the Conflict Studies Research Centre, a group of experts in Eurasian security, said Ukraine may well already have knowledge of the design of Storm Shadow missiles but using it without cooperation would be a “slap in the face to its coalition supporters”.
The reason Ukraine is only now getting access to the missiles’ blueprints has to do with politics, he said. “The United States is not willing to supply the interceptors for Patriot missile systems, so there’s a gap in Ukraine’s air and missile defences, which Russia has been exploiting.”
He added: “European partners are taking up the task of making sure that Ukraine can prevail in the war, and a major part of that is ensuring that it can strike into Russia.”
Vassil said British and French willingness to transfer classified missile-production knowledge sets a potentially important precedent for future allied cooperation. “But it remains uncertain whether this will have an impact on Washington’s posture regarding Patriot interceptors,” he said.
How fast can Ukraine scale up production of Storm Shadow missiles?
France and the UK have expressed hope that they can help Ukraine set up a production line by the end of the year.
However, estimates suggested a new batch of cruise missiles of this complexity could take about two years from contract award to delivery, according to Vassil, who added that establishing production will be a challenging endeavour and will most likely continue to depend on a complex international supply chain.
Storm Shadows also incorporate some sensitive US technologies, meaning some aspects of supply or transfer may still require US approval and “it remains uncertain how this will apply to Ukrainian production”, he said.
There are also substantial security challenges. “Missile-production facilities inside Ukraine would present valuable targets for Russia and would have to operate under the continuing threat of Russian long-range missile and drone attacks,” Vassil continued.
“Protecting production sites, dispersing manufacturing and maintaining supplies of critical components could, therefore, become almost as important as obtaining the technical information itself.”

Ukraine returns 10 servicemen its own records had marked missing in action
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-24
15:10:40 UTC
00:10:40 KST

Ukraine brought a small group of servicemen home from captivity on 24 August, its Independence Day, and every one of them had been carried as missing in action, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy announced. The men crossed back through Belarus as a separate stage of the exchange now under way. Ukraine's prisoner-of-war agency later set out who they were.
Amid Russia's all-out war in Ukraine, prisoner swaps remain one of the few Ukrainian-Russian mechanisms still producing results while every negotiating track on territory and ceasefires stays deadlocked, which leaves each completed stage as the practical measure of what still passes between two governments that agree on nothing else.
Ten men Ukraine had listed as missing, not captured
President Zelenskyy said Ukraine was bringing back 10 of its soldiers through Belarus. They serve in the Armed Forces and the National Guard, and they defended the country in the Donetsk sector in the east. He called it a special stage of the exchange.
The Coordination Headquarters for the Treatment of Prisoners of War, the state body that runs Ukraine's exchanges, specified the details in the afternoon. The freed men hold the ranks of sergeant, soldier, and sailor. All 10 had been logged as missing rather than captured.
Two had been listed as missing since 2024, the other eight since 2025. The agency said the handover came out of talks run by its own exchange working group. It described the return as the second stage of the current exchange.
The first stage ran on 19 August and brought back 103 servicemen.
Locating Ukrainian captives inside Russia or the occupied territories is often difficult, as is verifying their identities, because Russia withholds data on captured soldiers and civilian hostages. Former detainees describe beatings, electric shocks, mock executions, and refusals of medical care, and civilians held without trial report the same treatment as the soldiers.
Roughly 7,000 Ukrainian service members were in Russian captivity as of May 2026, with civilian detainees estimated at 10,000 to 20,000. Ukraine had returned 9,606 military personnel and civilians through exchanges by late June.

Empire State Building climbers kiss outside court after viral proposal
New York – A couple who climbed to the top of the Empire State Building and got engaged appeared in a New York court on Aug 24, before giving each other a lingering kiss in full view of the world’s media.
Ivan Kuznetsov, 32, and Angelina Nikolau, 33, face several charges after their viral stunt on July 1 when they clambered up an antenna at the peak of the 443m landmark.
During the climb, the pair, clad in black outfits with their faces covered, unfurled a banner that read: “When the power of love beats the love of power, the world knows peace.”
On the top of the building, Kuznetsov went down on one knee and appeared to propose to Nikolau, before they kissed and embraced as news helicopters swirled around them.
At the brief hearing on Aug 24, the pair each wore black leather jackets with jeans and stood quietly holding hands behind their lawyers.
Outside the courthouse, they embraced one another with a deep, 10-second kiss in front of a pack of journalists and onlookers.
The couple have built a huge online following for their illegal climbing exploits and starred in the Netflix documentary Skywalkers: A Love Story, which showed them scaling Malaysia’s Merdeka 118 – the world’s second tallest building.
Facing US charges including reckless endangerment, burglary and criminal mischief, they have defended their latest climb as “art” in a series of Instagram posts.
“Whatever happens in court, we will respect the process and accept the consequences of our choices,” the pair, who have not entered a plea, wrote online.
A further hearing was scheduled for Sept 29.
The Empire State Building has an observation deck open to the public that offers stunning views of New York, but access to higher points is forbidden. AFP

Ukraine Torches Three Ozon Mega-Warehouses, Hits MiG-29, as Drone Forces Hit 66 Targets in One Night
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-24
15:09:29 UTC
00:09:29 KST

- Category
- War in Ukraine
Ukraine Torches Three Ozon Mega-Warehouses, Hits MiG-29, as Drone Forces Hit 66 Targets in One Night
Ukrainian strike drones hit three major Ozon logistics centers across southern Russia, igniting large fires at facilities with a combined warehouse area of more than 314,000 square meters, according to photos and videos published by the OSINT community Exilenova+ on August 24.
The strikes formed part of a much broader Ukrainian operation deep behind Russian lines. Robert “Madyar” Brovdi, commander of Ukraine’s Unmanned Systems Forces, said his units successfully engaged 66 Russian targets during the night, including a MiG-29 fighter jet, four radar systems, military facilities and vessels linked to Russia’s shadow fleet.
We bring you stories from the ground. Your support keeps our team in the field.
“Birds of the Unmanned Systems Forces successfully struck 66 enemy targets in the operational depth of the enemy rear on the night of August 24,” Brovdi said.
Among the most significant targets, according to the commander, was another Russian MiG-29 near Dolotinka in Russia’s Rostov region.
“Among the sensitive targets was another MiG-29 [Dolotinka, Rostov region, Russia] and four radar systems: two Kasta-2E2 units, a Nebo-SV radar [all in Russia’s Rostov region] and an ST-68 radar [Rozdolne, Crimea],” Brovdi said.
He also reported the destruction of a base used by Russia’s SOBR special police forces in occupied Strilkove in Ukraine’s Kherson region, as well as strikes against energy infrastructure across Russian-occupied Ukrainian territory.
Two vessels associated with Russia’s shadow fleet—a tanker and a bulk carrier—were also hit in the Black Sea, Brovdi said. Eleven Russian temporary deployment points were struck across occupied parts of the Zaporizhzhia, Donetsk and Luhansk regions.
Three Ozon logistics centers were among the most visible targets of the overnight campaign.
The largest was a warehouse complex near Tyube in Russia’s Dagestan region, covering approximately 130,000 square meters. The site serves as a major logistics hub for northern Dagestan and lies roughly 800 to 900 kilometers from Ukraine’s state border.
A major fire erupted following the strike, with local residents reporting that the glow from the blaze could be seen from as far as 10 kilometers away.
Another Ozon logistics center was targeted in Nevinnomyssk, in Russia’s Stavropol region. The facility covers approximately 93,514 square meters.
The third site was an Ozon warehouse near Enem in Adygea, close to the border with Russia’s Krasnodar region. The complex covers about 91,200 square meters. A large fire developed at the facility after the attack.
Ozon is one of Russia’s largest online marketplaces and operates a sprawling logistics network comparable in function to major Western e-commerce platforms.
An investigation earlier found that Russian troops fighting in Ukraine had repeatedly ordered body armor, thermal-imaging equipment, radios, drone batteries, signal boosters, FPV components and payload-release systems through Ozon. Drone-related products were ordered through Ozon particularly frequently.
Ukraine has already put seven of the ten largest logistics centers operated by Russian e-commerce company Wildberries, OZON rival, out of operation.
Wildberries facilities in Domodedovo and at the Koledino industrial park were among the sites affected. The Koledino facility, covering approximately 250,000 square meters, was the company’s largest warehouse by area.

Syria struggling to deal with attacks on security forces
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-24
15:07:39 UTC
00:07:39 KST

Breadcrumb
Syria struggling to deal with attacks on security forces
Although the intensity of military confrontations has declined across most of Syria, attacks targeting security and military forces continue to occur, following a pattern of smaller, asymmetric operations. These range from bus bombings and improvised explosive devices (IEDs) to individual assassinations and ambushes.
Available information indicates that a large proportion of these attacks are linked to cells affiliated with Islamic State group. Responsibility for other attacks remains unknown, amid speculation about involvement of groups linked to remnants of the Assad regime.
Since Assad’s ouster in December 2024, ISIS has called on its members to fight the new government led by President Ahmad al-Sharaa, which has joined the US-led international coalition against the organisation.
Overnight buses targeted
Incidents recorded over the past year reveal a clear focus on buses transporting security and military personnel, as they are targets that bring together large numbers of personnel at a specific time and place.
The most recent such attack occurred on Saturday, when a bus belonging to the Internal Security Forces hit an IED on a road in the Damascus countryside, injuring several security personnel.
This came two weeks after a passenger bus was bombed in Jaramana, near Damascus, killing a woman and injuring 13 people.
A similar incident occurred in northeastern Syria in May, when two soldiers were killed in an attack on a military transport bus.
The most high-profile attack came during Emmanuel Macron's visit to the country in July, when Damascus was hit by twin blasts close to the French president's hotel. The interior ministry blamed ISIS which it said had planted explosives in a vehicle and a rubbish container.
Rashid Hourani, a researcher at the Jusoor Centre for Studies, told The New Arab that the targeting of vehicles belonging to the interior and defence ministries reveals weaknesses in security procedures. He also pointed to the sectarian nature of some of the attacks, highlighting the targeting of areas with high Alawite and Christian populations.
A security source who requested anonymity told The New Arab that most bombings and attacks have increasingly focused on overnight buses because they are relatively easy targets. They also believe that requiring personnel to surrender their weapons while on leave may also have increased their vulnerability to attack.
The source suggests providing personnel with weapons or security protection while they are traveling, avoiding the wearing of military uniforms while on leave, and changing travel routes and schedules.
He warned that some attacks may be random and primarily intended to create confusion and embarrass the government.
Assassinations, ambushes
Security forces have also come under fire from assailants in areas of eastern and northern Syria in recent months.
The latest such incidents came on Friday when a soldier and a member of the security forces were killed in separate attacks in Hama and Aleppo.
In recent months, there have also been attacks targeting personnel while they were traveling or outside their duty stations. In May, an attack on a defence ministry facility in Damascus killed one soldier and injured 23 people. Meanwhile, ISIS claimed responsibility for an attack in Hasakah that killed two soldiers.
ISIS also claimed responsibility for detonating a sticky bomb targeting the car of the head of the Justice Department in Babila, Salah Ahmad al-Saleh, seriously injuring him.
The extremist group has intensified its attacks against government forces since the beginning of the year. 29 people, including 23 military personnel, were killed in more than 30 ISIS attacks between 17 February and 19 March. The attacks were concentrated primarily in Deir ez-Zour, Raqqa, and Aleppo, with other incidents recorded in Idlib, Hasakah, and Homs.
Shifting threats
In response, the Syrian authorities have intensified their campaigns against ISIS cells. The Interior Ministry announced earlier this month that it had arrested a senior military commander the Manbij countryside. Last July, the authorities announced operations in Aleppo and Latakia that resulted in the arrest of ISIS members and the seizure of weapons.
The ministry said in June that over a three-month period it had arrested 235 people on terrorism charges and thwarted seven attacks that it said ISIS had been planning.
Military experts partly attribute this to the sensitivity of the transitional period and the presence of operational gaps resulting from the process of integrating the Syrian Democratic Forces (SDF) and other local groups into the army and security forces.
The record of the past year reveals that armed groups have shifted towards trying to wear down government forces through low-level bombings, assassinations, and ambushes.
The most prominent vulnerabilities include the predictable routes and schedules of overnight buses, personnel being exposed while on leave, and the difficulty of controlling open terrain and remote areas.
Major Khaled Abdullah, director of the Interior Minister’s office, said in press statements that the defence and interior ministries have issued directives prohibiting the wearing of official uniforms outside working hours and strengthening security measures. He noted that security and military institutions are working on other solutions to reduce risks.

"Canada has been ripping off the United States of America for years," the president wrote in a post on his Truth Social account.
US President Donald Trump announced on Monday that the US would double tariffs on Canadian vehicles from 2027 as he accused Ottawa of "ripping off the United States of America for years."
In a post on his Truth Social account, Trump wrote: "On January First, 2027, Tariffs on all Cars, Trucks, both large and small, Automotive Parts, and Steel, will be increased to 50%."
Current US tariff rates on automobiles stand at 25% for non-US content.
The threats come amid a growing trade war between the two neighbours that hit a flash point on Friday after talks over a deal to avoid 50% duties on some Canadian goods collapsed as both sides accused each other of trying to implement last-minute changes.
Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said Canada had been forced to walk away from the "bad" deal as "we cannot accept what they've offered, and we will not give what they've asked."
The levies, which came into effect on Saturday, impact around $20 billion worth of Canadian goods.
Carney warned that Ottawa would match the US tariffs "dollar for dollar to protect our workers and businesses."
"Our response will be concentrated in sectors such as steel, dairy, appliances, agricultural equipment, pulp and paper, and electronics," Carney added in a speech on Saturday.
The Office of the United States Trade Representative described the breakdown in talks as a "missed opportunity" for Canada, which it said was maintaining a "prolonged retaliation" against the US.
"Despite the U.S. offer to Canada to receive the best treatment of any major exporter to our market, new demands and walk backs of other commitments by Canada have upended the careful balance reached in the past days," it said.
Trump's tariff strategy
On Monday, Trump also lashed out at what he called Canada's "ridiculously high tariffs" on US farmers and said the country would no longer be treated "like a state."
Trump has repeatedly suggested that Canada should become the US' "51st state" and said last week that Ottawa wanted "the benefits of being a State, without being one."
The American president has pursued an aggressive tariff policy during his second stint in the White House, raising levies on partners across the world. The administration argues that tariffs will boost US manufacturing and encourage domestic job growth while addressing what it sees as unfair trade rates.
Critics, however, say increasing duties are making life more expensive for American consumers and businesses while fostering widespread uncertainty among companies planning investments and supply chains.
